objective: Close issue #79's latency checkbox honestly: measure the one capture-to-card segment that has no number, and record the whole I6 budget with its gaps named. Two of three segments are measured today. Render (response receipt -> committed card) is asserted under 50 ms per golden fixture by overlay/test/renderBudget.test.tsx. Trigger->frame on the native stack is p95 32.8 ms in overlay/bench/results/2026-07-26-linux-arm64-headless-electron.json (ADR-0004). The SHELL's own segment -- the clipboard sample that first sees new item text, through createClipboardPipeline, to the VERDICT ShellState arriving at onState -- is unmeasured. (1) Add overlay/test/captureLatency.test.ts: drive createClipboardPipeline with a stub ClipboardSource and a stub postDiff resolving a golden verdict fixture immediately (no network), and measure per fixture the elapsed time from the pollNow() that observes the new item text to the VERDICT state reaching onState. Assert a 20 ms per-capture shell-overhead budget and log per-fixture timings as renderBudget.test.tsx does. (2) Write overlay/bench/results/2026-08-03-capture-to-card-budget.md: one row per segment with its number, source file, and measurement conditions, INCLUDING the two segments this stage does NOT measure, stated as not measured rather than estimated -- (a) the server /diff call, backend-owned, and (b) the CLIPBOARD_POLL_MS = 100 detection lag, a hard 0-100 ms (mean ~50 ms) charge against the 300 ms budget imposed by the polling design, since Electron exposes no clipboard-change event. (3) Index it in overlay/bench/results/README.md in the existing per-run style. Do NOT change CLIPBOARD_POLL_MS or anything under overlay/src: if the shell overhead exceeds budget, report it in the PR and leave the source alone -- retuning the poll interval is a separate stage with its own evidence.
constraints: Measurement only. No overlay/src change of any kind, including CLIPBOARD_POLL_MS.
The recorded artifact must name what it does not measure. A budget table that silently omits the server segment and reads as a passing 300 ms is a doctrine I5 violation, not a completed checkbox.
Timings come from the runner on the box that ran them; never hand-write a number into the record that no check produced.
Existing files in overlay/bench/results/ are append-only evidence (results/README.md line 4) -- add a new file and a new README section; never edit the 2026-07-26 run.
Stage PR uses 'Refs #79', never 'Fixes' (ADR-0008): TASK-210 has open stages after this one.

acceptance_criteria.text: overlay/test/captureLatency.test.ts measures, per golden verdict fixture, clipboard-sample-observes-item-text -> VERDICT ShellState delivered to onState, and asserts each is under the 20 ms shell-overhead budget; the full overlay suite passes.

The test exercises the real createClipboardPipeline composition (watcher + flow + state projection) with only the clipboard source and postDiff stubbed -- it does not re-implement or bypass the pipeline.

overlay/bench/results/2026-08-03-capture-to-card-budget.md tabulates every capture-to-card segment with number, source, and conditions, and explicitly marks the server /diff segment and the CLIPBOARD_POLL_MS detection lag as NOT measured by this stage.
The record states that no end-to-end p95 < 300 ms (I6) claim follows from this artifact alone, and names what would have to be measured to make that claim.
overlay/bench/results/README.md indexes the new record; the 2026-07-26 run file is byte-identical to its committed state.
Diff touches only the three in-scope files; overlay/src is unmodified.

rollback: git revert the stage commit; only a test and two evidence documents are removed, no product behavior changes.
